beats.story: Cliff's desk is coated in paperwork and bright morning sunlight. In the middle of the chaos sit two fluffy donuts from the mall bakery. A printer on the side desk chugs out the last of its job as I tentatively take my seat across from him. "Jolene!" His grin buzzes through me. "Apologies for the mess. I'm hoping you like the honey crullers to make up for it." He grabs the freshly printed docs, shoves them in the stapler, and plops them on the desk in front of me. Then he tilts his screen toward me, revealing the first slide of a PowerPoint. "So you can follow along." I slide the papers toward me and read the headline: "Communication in Business." "Can I keep this?
beats.story_cn: 克里夫的办公桌被文件堆和明媚的晨光彻底覆盖。在这片狼藉的正中央，摆放着两个从商场面包店买来的蓬松甜甜圈。一旁的打印机正哐当哐当地吐出最后几页文件，我试探性地在他对面坐下。“乔琳！”他的笑容仿佛带着电流穿过我。“抱歉这里一团糟。希望你喜欢蜜糖吉拿圈，就当赔罪了。”他抓起刚打印好的文件，塞进订书机，啪一声放在我面前的桌上。接着他把屏幕转向我，露出PPT的第一页幻灯片。“这样你就能跟上进度了。”我把文件拉过来，读着标题：“商业沟通”。 “这个我能留着吗？”

He says it teasingly, but the praise makes my heart expand anyway. "Pretty much.

He stands, splays his arms dramatically, and announces, "Effective communication in the workplace has three key cornerstones . . ." As he continues, my eyes drift from the monitor to the yellow legal pad sitting open beneath it covered in Cliff's neat, boxy handwriting. On the top I see the words: Employees to support. My own name catches my eyes like a snare. Next to it, the only words legible are isolation, colleagues, and help her feel safe.
beats.story_cn: 他哂笑道：“你不是说盼我出息吗？学生能蹦多高，全看老师拉多长。”鼻翼微张，嘴角却勾起一丝笑。他霍然起身，双臂戏剧性地一扬，高声道：“职场高效沟通的三大基石是……”滔滔不绝间，我的视线从电脑屏幕滑向下方那本摊开的黄色法律便笺簿——上面爬满了克莱夫那工工整整、方块似的字迹。顶端赫然写着：需扶持的员工。我的名字像捕兽夹般猝然入眼。旁边依稀可辨的字眼只有：孤立、同事、以及让她感到安全。

beats.story: Each word presses into me like a wound. Cliff pauses as he realizes where I'm looking. Instantly, he is sweeping the papers together into a giant pile. "Sorry, no offense -- just realized I've left a lot of my work papers on the desk." He stuffs the sheets into a folder identical to the maroon one I keep in my own drawer. "No need to apologize." I force my expression neutral. "I didn't mean to be snoopy." The irony is not lost on me. He shakes his head. "Nah, it's more that I don't want any distractions from the amazing show I'm putting on." "Impossible." His expression warms.
beats.story_cn: 字字如针，扎进心里。克莱夫瞥见我的目光所及，蓦然顿住。下一秒，他手忙脚乱地将纸张归拢成高高一摞。“抱歉，绝非有意——就是发现桌上落了不少工作文件。”他把那叠纸塞进一个文件夹，与我抽屉里那个栗红色的一模一样。“用不着道歉。”我强作平静。“我不是存心窥探。”这反讽，我岂会不懂。他摇头道：“哪儿的话，主要是不想让杂事扰了我的精彩演出。”“绝无可能。”他神色一暖。

beats.story: "Hey, Jolene, you really did do a great job at the conference yesterday." "Thanks," I say, still forcing myself not to look at the maroon folder in his arms. "I was a little nervous at first, but I'm glad I didn't fumble too much." "I didn't notice any fumbling." He gestures toward his monitor. "But this show will help strengthen your skills. Which leads me to the second foundation of communication: body language." He swipes his hand across his body, fingers wiggling like he's in a boy band. When I don't laugh, his expression drops. "What's up? Why are you looking at the talent like they've upset you?" I can't stop thinking about that damn folder -- all the notes he makes for everyone, the individual meetings, the donuts. I swallow.
beats.story_cn: “乔琳，昨天大会你可真出彩。”“多谢。”我应道，目光死死钉在他怀中的栗色文件夹上。“起先有点慌，幸亏没演砸太多。”“砸？我看挺好。”他朝屏幕一指。“不过这场演出能帮你精进技艺。这就带出了沟通的第二块基石：肢体语言。”他夸张地挥臂划过身前，十指如男团舞者般扭动。见我毫无反应，他笑容骤敛。“怎么回事？干嘛一副我欠你钱的表情？”我满脑子都是那个该死的文件夹——他给每个人整理的笔记、私下约谈、还有那些甜甜圈。喉头一哽。

beats.story: Cliff's eyes widen with surprise, like he's been caught doing something other than being a total tool with a PowerPoint. "Jolene, kissing ass isn't a good look." "I'm being serious." I look straight into his eyes, hoping he can tell how much I mean it. Cliff stares back, something strange brewing behind his expression. Then he looks away sharply toward the window. The mood has quickly turned weird, so I say, "Doesn't it ever get to you, though? Dealing with office fucks and evaluating them on their personalized levels of bullshit?" His mouth curls upward. "I mean, yes, I can think of times where people's bullshit in the office does annoy me." He stares at me again pointedly. I bow my head.
beats.story_cn: 克利夫惊讶地睁大眼睛，像被撞见正在做除却扮演"只会用PPT的工具人"之外的其他事。"乔琳，拍马屁可不太体面。""我是认真的。"我直视他的眼睛，希望他能看出我有多当真。克利夫回视着我，神情里有些异样的暗流涌动。接着他猛地扭头望向窗外。气氛迅速变得古怪，于是我开口道："处理办公室里那些破事，应付各人不同程度的扯淡，难道从没让你烦过吗？"他嘴角扬起："我是说，确实，我想得出好几次被办公室那帮人的破事惹毛的时刻。"他又刻意地盯着我。我垂下了头。

beats.story: "Oh yes, I know I'm annoying. But anyway, it's cool you've found something you're really good at. The world needs more people who think they can save it." It's tiny this time, but Cliff tenses again. Another look toward the window, the little golden flecks in his irises catching the light. "Jolene, I . . ." His eyes shift and he shakes his head, like he's physically pushing a thought away. "We should get back to it." As he shuffles toward his mouse to wake up the monitor again, my eyes drift toward the windowsill where he'd been gazing.
beats.story_cn: "哦是，我知道我挺招人烦。不过说真的，能找到一件自己真正擅长的事，挺酷的。这世界正需要更多自以为能拯救它的人。"这次只是微微一顿，但克利夫又绷紧了。他再次望向窗外，虹膜里细小的金色斑点捕捉着光线。"乔琳，我……"他眼神游移，摇了摇头，仿佛在物理上推开某个念头。"我们该回去工作了。"他蹒跚着挪向鼠标，唤醒显示器，我的目光却飘向他曾凝视的窗台。

beats.story: "Now that sounds like you." But there's still some tension creasing at the corners of his eyes. How can he read me so well, so often? My eyes dart again to the maroon folder sitting on his desk, and I think of that little note again: help her feel safe. I hear myself say, "I don't really like who I was back then." I instantly regret my words. It's far too close to the bone. But Cliff nods and leans an inch closer across the desk. "Well, I don't know what you were like then -- aside from that you grew up dreaming of working at Supershops, of course -- but the Jolene of now is pretty great." His words are like a warm blanket. It's not much, but it still feels like a small piece of the weight on my shoulders has been lifted.
beats.story_cn: “这语气才像你。”但他眼角的褶皱里仍有一丝紧绷。他为何总能如此轻易、如此频繁地看穿我？我的目光再次瞟向他桌上那个栗色的文件夹，那张小纸条上的字句又浮现脑海：让她感到安全。我听见自己说：“我不太喜欢那时候的自己。”话音刚落便已后悔，那未免太戳心了。但克里夫点了点头，隔着办公桌朝这边倾近了一英寸。“嗯，我不知道你过去怎样——除了你从小梦想在‘超级商店’工作，这点当然知道——但现在的乔琳相当出色。”他的话语像一条温暖的毛毯。虽只是轻言片语，肩上那沉甸甸的负担，却仿佛真的卸下了一小块。

beats.story: "Want to get back to it?" he offers. "After we finish, I can draw out the Kidstreet studio set for you. It was way different from how it looked on TV." "That would be lovely." We finish the presentation without further interruption, and Cliff brings his A game to the performance. I can't help being charmed by his commitment. But the whole time one thought presses the back of my mind: If only we didn't have matching maroon folders. When I return to my workstation, a new email already sits in my inbox. From: Clifford Redmond To: Gregory Hall Subject: Quick meeting? Hello, After some initial meetings with employees, I'd love to meet and discuss the direction my reports seem to be heading.
beats.story_cn: “想继续吗？”他提议道。“结束后，我可以给你画出‘童街’工作室的布景图。它和电视上看到的截然不同。”“那太好了。”演示得以继续，未再受打扰。克里夫全力以赴，表现堪称完美。我不禁为他这份投入的魅力所折服。但整个过程中，一个念头始终在脑后萦绕：可惜我们用的是同款栗色文件夹。当我回到自己的工位时，收件箱里已躺着一封新邮件。发件人：克利福德·雷德蒙德；收件人：格雷戈里·霍尔；主题：开个短会？你好，在与员工们初步沟通后，我希望与您会面，讨论一下我下属们似乎正在发展的方向。

All the shit inside me hardens. How could he go straight to Gregory after that meeting? What could he be saying about me? I shouldn't have been so loud, so myself, in front of him. GREGORY: How is 4 pm? I'll have Rhonda book a meeting room. CLIFF: Perfect.
beats.story_cn: 我还有点敏感事务要谈——关于如何在必修课里管理员工，说不定对公司有好处。我五脏六腑都绷成了石头。会议刚散，他怎么能直接去找格雷戈里？会说我什么？我不该在他面前那么大声，那么毫不掩饰。格雷戈里：下午四点怎么样？让朗达订会议室。克利夫：完美。

I rack my brain, replaying every single thing I said in Cliff's office. Did I joke too much? Did I not listen to the presentation well enough? Or did my comment about high school make Cliff decide to look me up after all?
beats.story_cn: 巧得可怕。克利夫和格雷戈里的日程表上同时出现一场会议。就订在我身后这间董事会室——凯特琳刚才溜进去打电话的那间。我绞尽脑汁回放克利夫办公室里我说过的每句话：玩笑是不是过火了？报告是不是没听仔细？还是关于高中那段闲谈，反而让克利夫决定要查我背景？

If he's going to tell Gregory about my anxiety, or my behavior in our sessions, or anything else that will affect my life here -- I need to hear it with my own ears. If Cliff knows about what happened . . . No, I can't even think about that.

beats.story: But what are Mr. Cliff's ideas? What after that meeting could they be discussing? The door clicks open behind me. Caitlin emerges with her shoulders slumped, phone in hand. And an idea hits. It would be such a simple move. I look down at my phone sitting on my desk. I can't be in the room, but my phone can. Sometimes to really play the game, you need to take a bit of risk.
beats.story_cn: 但克利夫先生的主张究竟是什么？那场会议后他们究竟在讨论什么？身后的门咔哒一声开了，凯特琳耷拉着肩膀走出来，手里握着手机。一个念头突然闪过——这招其实再简单不过。我低头看向桌上自己的手机。我人进不了那间屋子，但我的手机可以。有时候想玩转这场游戏，总得冒点险。
